headline: Last session: Nifty gained 75 points while Sensex slipped into red; smallcaps remained in focus amid global trade concerns.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 22 September.

why: Nifty 50 managed to gain 75 points despite the Sensex slipping into the red during the last session.
CITI expressed concerns over potential additional U.S. tariffs, weighing on global trade sentiment.
Crypto-related stocks tumbled 10% following setbacks related to the CLARITY Act.
Investors remained focused on FII activity and crude oil price fluctuations as key market drivers.
whatHappening: Ghaziabad traders announced a shift to cash-only transactions from October 15 over UPI MDR fee disputes.
India and New Zealand are nearing the implementation of a Free Trade Agreement to boost global trade.
Delhi Airport's third runway is scheduled to reopen on September 20 after a major revamp.
German and European industries are studying possibilities of shifting production bases to other countries.

summary: The Indian market ended the last session on a mixed note as Nifty rose 75 points while Sensex faced pressure. Global trade concerns and domestic UPI fee disputes dominated headlines, alongside a major crash in crypto-related stocks. Markets are currently closed for the weekend and will resume operations on Tuesday, September 22.
